centered_carrier_certificate.center: Put x=lambda-log(a) and u_N=log(a/N), so log(N)=log(a)-u_N. Writing s_*'=c+ib and s_*''=c_x+ib_x gives the exact identities R=-s_*'x-c*u_N and R_x=-s_*''x-c_x*u_N+i*b*u_(N,x).
centered_carrier_certificate.correction_rows: In the centered variable, C=c_0+c_1*x+c_2*x^2 and D=d_0+d_1*x+d_2*x^2, where c_0=1+rho_1*log(a)+rho_2*log(a)^2, c_1=rho_1+2rho_2*log(a), c_2=rho_2, d_0=rho_(1,x)*log(a)+rho_(2,x)*log(a)^2, d_1=rho_(1,x)+2rho_(2,x)*log(a), and d_2=rho_(2,x).
centered_carrier_certificate.rate_defect: Put delta=chi_N-i*b*u_N. Then Q=(R+delta)C+D and N=R*Q+R_x*C. The existing physical estimate is |delta|<4h^2, but no estimate is used in this algebraic gate.

coefficient_certificate.leading_coefficient: The top coefficient is exactly p_5=i*rho_2*(X_T+V_p)*(s_*')^2. Hence the degree-five channel vanishes on the total-value fibre X_T+V_p=0; this is a degree reduction, not a remainder bound.
coefficient_certificate.observation_rows: For any real f=(f_V,f_N,f_A,f_Q), let F_f=f_V*C+f_N*N+f_A*A+f_Q*Q. Use alpha=(N_(p,xi),V_(p,xi),-Q_(p,xi),-A_(p,xi)) and beta=(N_p+A_(T,x),X_T+V_p,-Q_p-X_(T,x),-A_T-A_p). Then P_lin=F_alpha+i*x*F_beta.
coefficient_certificate.two_channel_factorization: For R=r_0+r_1*x and R_x=t_0+t_1*x, every F_f factors exactly as F_f=C*U_f+D*V_f. Here V_f=f_N*R+f_Q and U_f=f_N*[R(R+delta)+R_x]+f_Q(R+delta)+f_A*R+f_V. Thus four physical carrier polynomials reduce to the two correction channels C and D.
coefficient_certificate.uv_recurrence: Writing U_f=u_0+u_1*x+u_2*x^2 and V_f=v_0+v_1*x, put g_0=r_0(r_0+delta)+t_0, g_1=r_1(2r_0+delta)+t_1, g_2=r_1^2. Then u_0=f_Ng_0+f_Q(r_0+delta)+f_Ar_0+f_V, u_1=f_Ng_1+(f_Q+f_A)r_1, u_2=f_Ng_2, v_0=f_Nr_0+f_Q, and v_1=f_Nr_1.

ideal_certificate.boundary: The actual correction channels can restore degrees four and five. The ideal reduction is a scale guide, not an exact deletion of C-1 or D.
ideal_certificate.contact_polynomial: On X_T+V_p=0 and A_T+A_p=0, the correction-free leading polynomial is quadratic: P_lin=N_(p,xi)-i*A_p*u_(N,x)+i[N_p+A_(T,x)-Q_(p,xi)]x+X_(T,x)x^2/2.

ideal_certificate.specialization: At C=1, D=0, s_*'=-i/2, s_*''=0, delta=0, and b=-1/2, one has R=Q=i*x/2 and N=-x^2/4-i*u_(N,x)/2. The induced observation identities are A_p=Q_p, A_(p,xi)=Q_(p,xi), and V_(p,xi)=2A_p.

morse_amplitude_certificate.cprime_formula: For z!=0, c'_(P,r)(y)={z*J*W_P'(v)-W_P(v)+W_P(1)}/[r*sqrt(alpha)*z^2]. With g=t*lambda/2-sigma, this equals {exp(S)[zJ^2(P'+gP)/v+(zJJ'-J)P]+exp(S(lambda_0))P(lambda_0)}/[r*sqrt(alpha)*z^2], where lambda_0=log(alpha/r).
morse_amplitude_certificate.definitions: For u_0=alpha/r, lambda=log(u_0v), S(lambda)=t*lambda^2/4-sigma*lambda, z=sgn(v-1)sqrt(2[v-1-log v]), and J=dv/dz, put W_P(v)=exp(S(lambda))*P(lambda)*J(v). Then b_(P,r)(y)=sqrt(alpha)W_P(v)/r and y=sqrt(alpha)z.
morse_amplitude_certificate.mode_dependence: At fixed xi the same physical P_lin is used for every Poisson mode. Mode dependence enters only through lambda_0=log(alpha/r), the Morse endpoints, and the common phase. Thus the saddle audit is one second-order differential operator sampled on the logarithmic mode lattice, not six unrelated moment amplitudes.
morse_amplitude_certificate.saddle_formula: The removable saddle value is c'_(P,r)(0)=exp(S(lambda_0))/[2r*sqrt(alpha)] times {P''+(2g_0+1)P'+[g_0^2+g_0+t/2+1/6]P}(lambda_0), with g_0=t*lambda_0/2-sigma.
morse_amplitude_certificate.zero_boundary: Neither P_lin(lambda_0)=0 nor the displayed saddle operator vanishes identically. Any zero or discrete-difference gain must be proved from the physical coefficients and mode coupling.
